Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) re-aggravated his injury against the Giants and it will be “business as usual” with him in practice this week.
items.text: In other words, look for a lot of DNPs and limited sessions that don’t really matter, then a Friday decision at the end of the week. The Jaguars certainly could decide they have the luxury of resting Tuten against the Titans in Week 12. Chris Rodriguez could be either a viable RB2 or a useless FLEX play by Friday, depending on how this situation shakes out. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Seth McGowan (hamstring) “will miss some time.”
items.text: McGowan exited in Week 11’s loss to the Texans and did not return to the game. The rookie seventh-rounder had been seeing an increased role as of late, rushing 26 times for 158 yards and two touchdowns in his last four games while adding two receptions. His absence should create a slight uptick in opportunities for Jonathan Taylor, who has had no more than 16 rush attempts in his last four games. We’ll likely get a better sense of how long McGowan could be out in the coming days, but for now, DJ Giddens appears next in line behind Taylor. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson will undergo season-ending ankle surgery.
items.text: Ferguson tried multiple times to make his way back from the ankle injury that has sidelined him since Week 3. Initially expected to return in Week 9, Ferguson suffered a hamstring injury in practice that further delayed his return, but it doesn’t sound like his ankle ever fully healed in light of today’s news. Ferguson’s season comes to an end after just three games. The second-year tight end turned in an impressive 6-54-1 line in Week 2 against the Giants, but saw just three targets over his other two games. items.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Commanders are Brandon Aiyuk’s “most likely” landing spot.
items.text: The ink on the release wasn’t even given time to dry before Aiyuk was connected to the same team he was connected to all offseason. He’ll likely wind up with a spot on the Commanders practice squad. Given the lengthy layoff, we probably don’t need to imagine Aiyuk suiting up in Week 12 as a destined outcome, but it could be sooner rather than later. - Rivers McCown

items.title: 49ers released WR Brandon Aiyuk.
items.text: Took them long enough, you might say before you were pedanted by those who would tell you things like “Aiyuk had to report to actually be released.” It should be noted that Aiyuk must clear waivers since this is after the trade deadline, but nobody is expected to assume his contract. Anyway, Aiyuk will be free to pursue free agency and it sounds like we have another blurb to write about that almost instantly, funny how that works. The 28-year-old will look to continue his career elsewhere, perhaps somewhere in the greater Washington D.C. area. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy said Kenneth Walker (groin) will “remain the starter” when he returns.
items.text: Rookie Emmett Johnson has rushed for 45-206-1 in two games without Walker this season, which has led some to wonder what role Walker could have when he returns from his groin injury. Walker, who currently ranks fifth in the league in rushing yards (872) and leads the league in yards per carry (5.5) could return as early as this Thursday when the Bills play host to the Chiefs on Thanksgiving, and from the sound of things, it would be safe to say he will be in line for plenty of work. items.title: FOX Sports’ Jay Glazer reports the 49ers signed President of Football Operations and GM John Lynch to an extension.
items.text: Lynch joined the Niners as general manager in 2017 and was promoted to President of Football Operations in 2023. Since his arrival, the Niners have emerged as one of the better-run organizations in the league. Under Lynch, the Niners have gone 91-68 in the regular season while making two trips to the Super Bowl and four trips to the NFC Championship Game. items.title: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Jalen Coker has cleared concussion protocol.
items.text: Coker was checked in the fourth quarter after taking a hard hit from Roquan Smith, but it looks like he’ll be fine to use against the Buccaneers on Monday night. With all 32 teams active, it may be time to capitulate and put Coker back on the WR3 line. He has not cleared 50 yards since Week 6. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Trevor Etienne’s production and Tre Tyus’ special teams value make it “challenging” to find a spot for Jonathon Brooks.
items.text: Brooks, who is on injured reserve due to a groin injury, has eight days to be activated or lost for the season. The 23-year-old back practiced in full last week all three times only to not be activated. It would be great news for Chuba Hubbard if this continued, as the team has shown little interest in using Etienne in a real role in the backfield. - Rivers McCown
